description: §23.5.5 — a foreign-code construct (`use foreign:ml` sidecar, §23.4) with NO `capabilities=` on any ancestor `<program>` is governed by the empty (declare-nothing) set, so the presence-nudge W-FOREIGN-UNDECLARED-CAPABILITY fires (Info). The lint nudges the author to declare the scope's intended capability surface. It is PRESENCE-only (opacity bound §23.2.3 — it never inspects the foreign interior). Advisory (Info) — never blocks the build. CODE UPDATED S356 r4, and this case is the one that MOVED rather than renamed: the co-occurring error used to be `E-FOREIGN-SIDECAR-NOMINAL` ("the §23.4 sidecar runtime is unbuilt"), but this file declares no nested `<program name="ml">` AT ALL — the `lang="ts"` is on the top-level `<program>` — so what is actually wrong with it is that `use foreign:ml` names a sidecar nothing declares. That is `E-FOREIGN-010` (§23.4, normative since the section landed, first emitted S356 r4). The retired code was covering an unresolved reference under a Nominal banner, which is exactly why retiring it needed a real closure rather than a deletion.
rationale: §23.5.5: the compiler SHALL emit W-FOREIGN-UNDECLARED-CAPABILITY (Info) when a foreign construct is governed by an empty capability set. Here no ancestor declares `capabilities=` → empty → the lint fires as Info (partitions into result.warnings; CLI exit driven by the co-occurring E-FOREIGN-010, an Error). §23.4 normative: "The `name` in `use foreign:name` MUST match the `name=` attribute of a nested `<program>` declared within the same top-level `<program>`. An unresolved name SHALL be a compile error (E-FOREIGN-010)." No nested `<program>` exists here, so it fires. E-NESTED-PROGRAM-CONTEXT-NOMINAL does NOT: that code refuses a nested-`<program>` DECLARATION, and there is none to refuse. No E-SCOPE-001 — the sidecar fn names stay in scope by design, so a `predict(...)` call site does not double-report.
